To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) SP-A exists predominantly as smaller (dimeric) oligomers when bound to lung surfactant lipid micelles and 2) Mini-B interacts with SP-A, and the degree of interaction is dependent on the lipid headgroup.

(i) SP-A is a flexible molecule, which exists in a variety of oligomeric states in water and in the presence of surfactant lipids, (ii) SP-A binds to Mini-B and may undergo further structural rearrangement, and (iii) the nature of the lipid headgroup affects the degree of Mini-B–SP-A interaction.
SP-A exists predominantly in oligomeric forms when bound to lung surfactant lipid mimics, and that it interacts with the SP-B fragment Mini-B in a lipid dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating SP-A’s interactions with lung surfactant lipids and Mini-B, in order to better understand its role in surfactant function.
the structural and dynamic properties of surfactants in solution.
elucidating the structure of SP-A in the presence of model lung surfactant lipids, and with probing the interaction of SP-A with Mini-B in the presence of the same lipids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP-A exists predominantly as smaller aggregates in lung surfactant and that it interacts with SP-B in the presence of lipid micelles.
SP-A’s interactions with Mini-B and lung surfactant lipids are complex.
the interaction of SP-A with Mini-B is not dependent on the type and concentration of lipid micelles, but the degree of interaction is affected by the type of micelles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the octadecamer is the predominant oligomeric state for SP-A in aqueous solution, the protein is capable of forming smaller oligomers in the presence of lung surfactants.
SP-A’s oligomeric state in the presence of lung surfactants is dependent on both the type and concentration of the lipid, as well as on the type of micellar environment.

SP-A’s structure and interactions with other components of lung surfactants are strongly dependent on lipid composition, as would be expected for a protein whose primary role is to modulate the physical properties of lung surfactation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SP-A is not necessarily octadecametric in its interactions with surfactant components and that the protein is capable of undergoing further conformational changes upon interaction with other surfactant components.
SP-A is likely to interact with lung surfactant lipids as a smaller oligomer than the octadecamer.
the interactions of surfactant proteins with lung surfactant lipids may be more complex than previously appreciated.
